title: Aurum Alpha object reference
description: standards/026-blob-storage.md BS4: what an application stores about a stored object, in a row of its own database that owns the object. The reference is bucket-agnostic: a key, a content type, a size, a checksum, a status and timestamps, and never a URL, a bucket name or an endpoint - those are configuration (BS2), and a URL stored in a row is a credential or a hostname persisted for the life of the row. The row is the source of truth: an object in the bucket with no row is an orphan (BS8), and a row whose object is absent is a pending upload (BS6) or a defect. The shape is closed so that a URL, a bucket or an internal key cannot enter it under another name. Ids and timestamps are the identifiers contract's; the tenant id is the observability contract's vocabulary. schema_version 1 - evolves additively per PC6.

mediaType.description: BS6. An IANA media type, lowercase, type and subtype only: image/png, application/pdf. No parameters and no wildcard - a wildcard is a policy shorthand that re-expands on load and is refused for the same reason 070 RB6 refuses one.

checksum.description: BS6. SHA-256 of the object as storage reports it at confirm, lowercase hex, prefixed with the algorithm: sha256:<64 hex> for an object written in one part; sha256-<n>:<64 hex> for a multipart object, where the value is the composite the S3 API defines over its n parts. Never an ETag, which is not a digest of the bytes for a multipart object and is not promised to be one for any object.

filename.description: BS3, BS5. The name the uploader gave the file, kept as display metadata and used to build Content-Disposition at read time. Never part of the key. No path separators, no control characters; length bounded so it fits a header.

schema_version.description: PC6. The version of this shape.

id.description: BS3, BS4. The object's public id: a UUIDv7 minted by the server at intent time, equal to the key's final segment. This is what the owning row references and what an API exposes; the key itself is never an API value.

key.description: BS3. The object's key in the service's bucket, in the grammar key.schema.json fixes. Bucket-agnostic: the same key names the object in every environment's bucket.

tenant_id.description: BS10. The owning tenant's public id, present wherever the service is tenant-scoped and equal to the key's first segment. The isolation column 025 SD5 requires on a scoped table; the row, not the key prefix, is what the isolation check reads.

content_type.description: BS6. Declared at intent, admitted by the upload policy, and confirmed against the bytes by the server's own sniff before the row becomes stored. Set on the stored object and re-asserted on every presigned read (BS5); the client's declaration is never recorded unverified.

size_bytes.description: BS6. Declared at intent and verified against what storage reports at confirm; bounded above by the policy's max_size_bytes and, absolutely, by the S3 API's single-object ceiling of five tebibytes.

checksum.description: BS6. Declared at intent, verified against what storage reports at confirm. The value that makes a later integrity check possible without trusting the storage's own accounting.

original_filename.description: BS3, BS5. Display metadata and the source of Content-Disposition. Optional: an object generated by the service has none.

status.description: BS6. pending: the intent row exists and the confirm has not succeeded; the object may or may not be in the bucket. stored: confirm verified size, checksum and content type against storage and the bytes. Only a stored object is ever served.

scan.description: BS7. The malware-scan posture of this object under its entity's policy. not_required where the policy says scan: false; otherwise pending from intent until the scan job records clean or infected. A presigned read is issued only for not_required or clean. infected: the object has been deleted from the bucket and the row records why it is gone.

created_at.description: IP4. When the intent row was written. The clock the orphan purge (BS8) reads a pending row against.

stored_at.description: IP4. When confirm succeeded. Present exactly when status is stored.

allOf.description: BS6. A stored row says when it was stored; a pending row cannot.
BS7. A scan verdict exists only for an object that was stored; a pending row is not_required or pending.
